lens: Prospective applicant — ambiguous result (simulated user lens)
reason: The reviewed applicant journey is thoughtfully structured: Join explains eligibility, evaluation and preparation; Apply separates draft saving from submission; recovery pauses writes and compares copies before a destructive choice. The supplied desktop and mobile homepage captures show coherent Precision Instrument hierarchy and a visible student action. Public content identifies student-led consulting and labels unpublished case-study proof honestly. The application review accurately discloses original-resume access rather than promising fully anonymous review. However, an unresolved submission acknowledgement can still degrade to an unhelpful generic error. More broadly, the passing intercepted-browser checks and isolated database race do not establish that a student can complete the hosted identity/upload/submission/status journey. I cannot give an unconditional world-class or release endorsement from this evidence. This is independent AI source/evidence review, not observed student success.

findings.evidence: After HTTP 500/502/503/504, unsuccessful reconciliation falls through to body.error or “The application could not be submitted.” Only thrown timeout/network errors receive the explicit unknown-receipt and safe-retry guidance. src/lib/client-fetch.ts:54-59 explicitly notes that failed/negative reconciliation cannot prove non-commit. The RPC catch at src/app/api/apply/route.ts:75-83 can produce 503 after an unknown acknowledgement. The supplied browser case at tests/e2e/application-reliability.spec.ts:206-229 covers a 500 followed by successful status confirmation, not exhausted/unavailable status reads.
findings.userImpact: A student whose write may have committed but whose status cannot be checked sees a generic failure or service-outage message without knowing whether they applied or whether clicking Submit again is safe.
findings.suggestedFix: When a potentially ambiguous server failure remains unconfirmed, show the same explicit unknown-receipt and duplicate-safe retry guidance used for timeouts, preserve answers, and add a focused browser case for 503/500 plus exhausted status failures.

notVerified: No staging environment, hosted integration or human study exists; actual Clerk sessions, RPC/RLS, upload storage and receipt email delivery were not exercised together.
No supplied authenticated application/recovery/status captures establish private-screen visual quality; those judgments are limited to source and synthetic tests.
The inspected logs show local intercepted Chromium checks and a two-session PostgreSQL initial-save race, not every save/upload/submit concurrency scenario.
Physical devices, Safari, Firefox and assistive-technology task completion remain unverified.
